devices/H6076.yaml.content: `max_hz_by_zones` carries concrete values (40/25/20 Hz) whose `source` is `toolkit-measured-other-sku`: they were measured on an H61A0, not on any H6076. `defaultRateHz()` (packages/govee/src/profiles.ts:339) takes this table whenever it is non-null and prefers it over `fallback_hz`, so an unqualified H6076 is capped by another SKU's ceiling rather than the 10 Hz fallback. If the real H6076 ceiling is lower (plausible: this is a floor lamp with a different LED count/PSU from the H61A0 strip), the pre-qualification default overdrives the unit until the wizard's step-13 sweep replaces it. Because `Measured.value` has no per-SKU guard in the loader/lint (profiles.ts only rejects `capabilities.segmented === true` from a non-hardware source), nothing stops this cross-SKU table from being applied as an H6076 value. Consider leaving the table null (`source: unmeasured`) until the H6076 sweep exists, or gating its use on qualification.

`product_material_segments.value` is `null` while `source` is `product-material` in both `devices/H6076.yaml` and `devices/H1A45.yaml`, contradicting the convention that a missing value uses `source: unmeasured` (as with `length_m`, `segment_chain`, `native_pixels_per_meter`, and the capability probes). The loader (`measured()` in profiles.ts:184) accepts any source with a null value, so this passes validation, but the `Measured` model documents source as provenance, so a null value has none. A consumer that branches on `measured.source !== 'unmeasured'` will treat these nulls as known values. For H6076, either record the claim as a value or set `source: unmeasured`. For H1A45, the receipt says spec 43 records no published segment count for the 20 m strip, so `source: unmeasured` is the correct label.

packages/analysis-client/vitest.config.t.content: `readdirSync(packages)` returns every entry in `packages/`, not just package directories. Non-package entries (e.g. `.DS_Store`, `README.md`, `.gitignore`, any file or stray folder) each become an `@autolight/<name>` alias pointing at a non-existent `<name>/src/index.ts`. This can mask genuine "module not found" errors with a confusing resolution attempt into a bogus path. The root `vitest.config.ts` guards against this with `readdirSync(workspaceSrc, { withFileTypes: true }).filter((e) => e.isDirectory())`; do the same here.

Vitest/Vite alias `find` values are prefix-matched, so the plain string alias `@autolight/foo` also rewrites deep imports like `@autolight/foo/subpath` to `<foo>/src/index.ts/subpath`, producing a wrong (non-existent) module path. The root `vitest.config.ts` deliberately places a regex subpath alias (`/^@autolight\/([^/]+)\/([^/]+)$/`) before the barrel aliases ("T-TRU-04 spine fix") so barrels never swallow `/subpath` imports. Mirror that ordering here, or use an exact-match regex for the barrel alias.

packages/ble/package.json.content: With `"type": "module"`, the package only exposes `main`/`types` and has no conditional `exports` map. Node/bundlers prefer `exports` when present, and its absence prevents any subpath or explicit ESM/CJS condition resolution for consumers of this scoped package. Sibling `@autolight/config` already declares an `exports` map; add one here for consistency and future-proof resolution.

There is no `files` allowlist, and `dist/` is listed in the repo `.gitignore`. With no `.npmignore` and no `files` field, npm falls back to `.gitignore` when packing, which would exclude `dist/` from the published tarball — leaving `main`/`types` pointing at non-existent files. Conversely, without the fallback the build output plus `src`/`tsconfig` would be published wholesale (TS config has no test exclusion, so compiled `*.test.js` land in `dist/`). Declare a `files` allowlist (or add an explicit `.npmignore`) so the published surface matches the build output.

packages/dj-core/src/beat-mapping.proper.content: The seek property loop can pass with a broken millisecond-threshold path. It only asserts `got === true` when the beat error alone exceeds the beat threshold (`errBeats > 0.5`), and only asserts `false` for the narrow region `errBeats < 0.4 && errorMs < 140`. There is no case that must be tripped by the ms branch (i.e. `errBeats <= 0.5` but `errorMs > 150`), so an `exceedsSeekThreshold` that drops the `beatsPerSecond`/ms check, or sets `seekThresholdMs` far too high, still satisfies every assertion. In addition, the 0.4–0.5 'dead zone' and the literal `140` (vs the real default 150) let up to ~20% error in `seekThresholdBeats`/`seekThresholdMs` slip through. Reference the defaults instead of magic literals and add a case that must trip the ms branch.

To make this test actually catching for the 'non-monotonic map' class it claims to guard, also assert strict growth (the output must span the grid, e.g. `b[last] > b[first]`).

The test name claims the two detectors 'agree at the boundary', but `isSeek` (a seconds threshold, 0.25 here) and `exceedsSeekThreshold` (a beats + ms threshold) are exercised completely independently and never compared. Either add a cross-check of their documented relationship or rename the test, otherwise the coverage claim is misleading.

packages/govee/src/index.test.ts.content: Test-validity flaw: the toolkit side of this "parity" proof is `StubBindingStream`, a hand-written reimplementation of the exact same arm-settle / newest-wins / no-resend / supersede-counting logic that `PacingStream` (NativeStreamEngine) implements. Because both sides are written from the same spec in the same process, the equality assertions (`toolkitSink.datagrams === nativeSink.datagrams`, matching `framesSent`/`framesSuperseded`) hold unconditionally even if the *real* `govee_toolkit` binding behaves differently (e.g. re-sends unchanged frames, doesn't coalesce, or orders arm/paint differently). The test therefore cannot detect divergence from the artifact it claims to compare against, and would still pass with a broken native engine as long as the stub copies the same bug. Consider asserting against independently recorded golden datagrams / the real binding (as the simulator test attempts), or at minimum add a case that the stub is deliberately configured to violate, so a regression in either side fails.
